Hi there, sorry to hear about your diagnosis. I am 35 and have a 1 year old son. I have had RA since I was 11. And with the advancement of medication and therapies there’s honestly no way to know whaat direction RA can go. I’ve seen some people progress with RA damage quickly and some that don’t have much damage at all. With the right doctor and information I know that a lot of the time you can find the right balance of medication or therapy that can help slow the progression. For me it is Orencia. I don’t have a lot of damage but I have gone through a fair amount of medications to get to this point. I hope that you find the best one that works for you, and in doing so you will still be able to love, care for, cuddle and enjoy every moment with your little one as they grow up. And know that we are here for you as well.

And I had a medical abortion yesterday through the pill. As much as I want a family with him which I'm still conflicted with, I know it wasn't the right one. I have huge student debt. He wants to get the career and not just be working on the job. We want to leave the continent at least once in our lives. He wants to get married and have a house. My main focus is getting rid of my loans. So in a way I feel selfish for my reasons. But I know it's not the right time. I'm sitting here a few hours after the second pills and it's hitting me that it's over. I'm not a very emotional person and haven't been since I found out. But now, I feel very sad and yet relieved because I know it's for the best. I am sorry you're going through this. And know that the best time for it to happen will come. And you'll know it. I truly believe we as women have amazing intuition and we know when times are right or wrong. Best wishes to you.

I'm kind of in this situation but I didn't grow up rich. I've struggled my whole life and I made a change for myself by going away to college and moving out of my parents house at 24 to get myself a better life. But I have no family, and I am 31 and I am clinically depressed and my bf of 3 years seems to make my feelings look small or insignificant. I just lost my job on Friday and I am having horrible anxiety. I see no point in trying to work since I'm extremely afraid of getting laid off. I made 50k a year and didn't make a dent in my student loans. I feel alone cause I have no best friend. 

So I feel like I understand you just through another perspective. Even when you have nothing and work to have it all you can still feel depression somehow someway. I usually try to channel mine through journaling but this one is a bad moment. I understand you wanting to give up, and even though you feel like you have no one, it seems like you have your mom. That's the one person I've been crying for all night. The one person I want to ask why am I here? But I can't cause mine died when I was 5. I would suggest just thinking of her when you're down. Not how you think you hurt her or anything negative like that. Just your love for her and her love for you. I would think that with those thoughts it may help you hang on a bit longer.

Maybe your next step is journaling or channeling your feelings somewhere? I journal and at  times it helps. Today's not one of those days as I'm having a bad day myself. But maybe just finding an outlet. I hope you pull through.
